transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood CSM), Nina Patel (Palisade Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Palisade Platform Eng), Leah Chen (Palisade Head of Product)

Summary section (auto): quick health read, surfaced cost spikes on 3/12 and 3/21, agreed pilot to exercise autoscaling rules and failover.

00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:06 Nina Patel: Nina here — hey Alex.
00:08 Marco Ruiz: Marco — morning. little late on my side but i am here.
00:12 Leah Chen: Leah here, thanks.
:-- 00:15 Alex Kim: Cool. Samir and Priya from our side on the call as well. main goals today — align on recent usage anomalies, go over cost drivers, and make sure the runbook for failover/dedicated fallback is actionable.
00:38 Priya Rao: I'll flag the three areas we saw: token distribution changes, bigger seq lengths during peak search, and an unfortunate pattern where a small percentage of requests bypassed prefix cache which jacked up token counts.
00:52 Marco Ruiz: yeah that prefix-cache thing — i think a deploy last week changed how we hashed session ids, so cache keys mismatched.
01:04 Nina Patel: that was the hypothesis, we rolled back but costs already spiked. can you show the raw numbers?
01:12 Alex Kim: Sure, we'll attach the CSV after the call — high level: on 3/12 we saw a 32% increase in token consumption hour-over-hour for two hours, and on 3/21 a sustained 22% for a four hour window. the unit cost over that period increased 18% because of longer sequences and more cold KV cache fills.
01:38 Priya Rao: to add, when the cache misses happened we saw concurrent KV cache re-population which increased latency by ~200ms P90 and forced more requests to fall back to the heavier model variant.
01:54 Leah Chen: So is that a configuration change we can make on our side, or do you recommend a Redwood config?
02:02 Priya Rao: Both. short term — maintain sticky session IDs so cache keys remain stable. medium — we can suggest a routing rule: route traffic with a small warmup window to Dedicated capacity during spikes so you hit reserved capacity rather than bursting on hosted pricing.
02:20 Marco Ruiz: dedicated vs hosted — we've been mulling Dedicated for months. main blocker is procurement and proving the SLO improvements justify the commit.
02:31 Samir Gupta: understood. one thing we can do is run a short pilot where we simulate your peak traffic against a dedicated pool and measure token burn and latency delta; that data tends to help procurement.
02:44 Nina Patel: timeline?
02:46 Alex Kim: we propose a two-week pilot: week one baseline (staging), week two run with dedicated pool + autoscaling rules.
02:54 Marco Ruiz: do you need any infra changes from us?
02:57 Priya Rao: just staging access and the traffic patterns — sample scripts are in the pilot doc. we'll run with your quantization settings and the same prompts so it's apples-to-apples.
03:08 Nina Patel: okay. about runbook — we need explicit steps for failover, rollback, and communication (pager, slack channel). we've had gaps there.
03:18 Alex Kim: we've drafted a runbook template for other retailers; we'll adapt it and share. It includes: detection thresholds (latency, error rate, token burn), decision matrix (when to switch routing policies), rollback steps, and a postmortem checklist.
03:33 Leah Chen: include contact escalation ladders — we need on-call names, not just generic roles.
03:38 Samir Gupta: absolutely, we'll add names and also optional automated steps if you have On-Call integrations.
03:45 Marco Ruiz: on security/compliance, procurement asked about VPC/private plane options and KMS. short answer?
03:52 Priya Rao: Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPCs and KMS integrations. we'll share the SOC2 report and a summary of our network model. note: small differences in audit logs retention depending on plan.
04:07 Nina Patel: can you confirm data residency — some EU customers require logs to stay in-region.
04:12 Priya Rao: yes, we have region pinning and audit log retention options per tenancy — we'll include that in the security pack.
04:20 Alex Kim: back to cost — we'll send the annotated billing by model and by day. also we'll propose a few optimizations: 1) prefix KV cache tuning, 2) suggestion of 8-bit quantized variant for high-volume low-accuracy routes, 3) smarter batching for lower-cost routes.
04:38 Marco Ruiz: quantization might change quality marginally — do you have quality regressions tracked?
04:43 Priya Rao: we run evals on prompts; we'll share a quick A/B delta for the suggested quantized model on a representative prompt set. no surprises expected but we'll validate.
04:55 Nina Patel: if we do a canary, what metrics should we watch?
05:00 Priya Rao: latency P95/P99, tokens per request, cache hit %, error rate, and business metric: conversion on recommendation. we'll provide dashboards.
05:12 Alex Kim: action items recap coming up. any other blockers?
05:16 Marco Ruiz: procurement wants a clear cost comparator: projected monthly bill Hosted vs Dedicated for X qps. can you make that conservative?
05:24 Alex Kim: yes — we'll provide three scenarios: steady-state, bursty-peaks, and worst-case. plus suggestion for minimum reserve size.
05:32 Leah Chen: who owns the actual runbook update?
05:35 Samir Gupta: Redwood will draft, Palisade will review and add contact names.
05:40 Nina Patel: good. also ask — the alerts we already push into datadog; can the Redwood traces integrate?
05:47 Priya Rao: yes we have a tracing hook and datadog export. we'll include the setup snippet.
05:54 Marco Ruiz: fine. next steps and timeline again?
05:58 Alex Kim: 1) send csv and cost breakdown by 2026-04-01; 2) Palisade grant staging access by 2026-04-03; 3) pilot kickoff scheduled w/in two weeks: propose 2026-04-13 for pilot start; 4) runbook draft to be shared 2026-04-06.
06:16 Nina Patel: sounds good. thanks everyone.
06:20 Alex Kim: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links to docs and the calendar invite for the pilot.
